summary.zh: 观众、规范认可和责任怎样改变公开与私下的互动。
summary.en: How audiences, approval from norms, and responsibility change public and private interaction.

body.zh: **我们的观点。** 两个人之间可能还站着一个看不见的第三方：同事、朋友、组织、围观者，或者双方自己认可的规则。饰／蔑提供对这些认可的不同依赖方式；观众、证据和行动后果又会改变两人的表达。 我们关心：谁需要一个说得过去的版本；谁替谁背书；谁会在公开场合拆台；两人私下的共识能否承担公开后的后果。共同口径可以服务协调，也可能成为遮蔽事实的工具，需要把实际行为一并写清。 **自拟场景。** 掮客准备了一套各方都能接受的分配说法，投机客直接说出谁拿得更多。这可以是拆台的笑点，也可以成为追问不对等分配的起点。若没有需要辩护的行为，不能仅凭一个人措辞直接就把其判成蔑。 **写作支点：** “他们私下知道什么？公开时又各自愿意承认多少？” 研究路径：印象管理与道德脱离。[S12](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.3.598)、[S13](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.71.2.364)。二者分别涉及呈现与自我约束，本方法没有把它们合并为饰／蔑的现成测量证据。
body.en: **Our view.** An invisible third party may stand between two people: colleagues, friends, an organization, onlookers, or rules both accept. Justification and Disregard describe different ways of relying on that approval. Audiences, evidence, and consequences can in turn change how the pair express themselves. We ask who needs a defensible account, who vouches for whom, who undercuts the other in public, and whether their private agreement can bear the consequences of becoming public. A shared account can aid coordination or conceal facts. The actual behavior must be described alongside it. **An invented scene.** The Broker prepares an explanation of the distribution that every party can accept. The Opportunist bluntly names who receives more. This can be a comic interruption or the start of questions about an unequal allocation. Without behavior that needs defending, direct wording alone cannot establish Disregard. **Writing prompts:** What do they know privately? How much is each willing to admit publicly? Research paths: impression management and moral disengagement. [S12](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.3.598), [S13](https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.71.2.364). These concern presentation and self-restraint respectively. This method does not combine them into ready-made measurement evidence for Justification and Disregard.
